title: NNQS-SCI: Tackling Trillion-Dimensional Hilbert Space with Adaptive Neural Network Quantum States
problem: Scaling NNQS to large chemical systems requires managing trillion-dimensional Hilbert spaces while preserving accuracy
motivation: Enable high-accuracy quantum many-body simulations on HPC platforms with trillion-dimensional state spaces
method: The approach combines neural networks—which learn patterns in quantum system behavior—with a filtering technique called Selected Configuration Interaction (SCI, which selects only the most important quantum states to simulate). Instead of calculating all possible states for large systems (which is infeasible), the system automatically chooses which ones to include based on their importance. It runs the Slater-Condon rules (the mathematical calculations for quantum interactions) in parallel across multiple processors and uses memory compression to efficiently handle the vast space of quantum states.
key_novelty: NNQS-SCI scales to 152 spin orbitals (representing over 10^14 possible quantum states) through adaptive configuration selection, which maintains accuracy without arbitrary limits.
contributions: NNQS-SCI architecture combining neural networks with exact SCI for accuracy
Parallelized Slater-Condon rules for efficient local energy computation
Adaptive SCI engine managing billions of configurations without space explosion
limitations: Limited to spin systems; scalability beyond 152 orbitals unclear; computational cost analysis not detailed
